original_question: Given two polytopes P and Q, when does there exist a polytope whose facets are each isomorphic to either P or Q, and when can such a polytope be finite?
target_in_paper: Best match: the paper’s open problem about the semiregular/facet-intransitive construction problem for abstract polytopes—namely, determining when two given abstract polytopes can occur as the two facet types of a higher-rank abstract polytope, and when such an example can be finite.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core existence question, the fact that two prescribed polytopes P and Q are the input data, and the secondary finiteness question. It also points in the right direction by asking for a higher-dimensional polytope built from prescribed facet types.
missing_details: The paper is about abstract polytopes, not convex/geometric polytopes in Euclidean space.
P and Q should be assumed to have the same rank (so they can serve as facets of a common higher-rank polytope).
The ambient object sought is an abstract (n+1)-polytope when P and Q are abstract n-polytopes.
The intended question is not merely that each facet is isomorphic to either P or Q, but that the higher-rank polytope has two facet types/orbits, represented by P and Q.
If the intended setting is the usual semiregular/facet-intransitive one, one should state the local incidence condition that each ridge is incident with one facet of each type.
Your draft omits the k-orbit context of the paper, especially that the motivating setting is non-regular abstract polytopes with controlled flag-orbit structure.
It does not specify whether P and Q are assumed regular, chiral, or arbitrary abstract polytopes; the paper’s nearby context matters here.
It does not specify what 'finite' means in this literature: finitely many faces/flags, not geometric boundedness.
It does not distinguish between existence in general and existence of finite examples.
It does not mention that the paper’s formulation is an open problem, not a theorem or classification result.
refined_question: Let P and Q be abstract n-polytopes of the same rank. Under what necessary and sufficient conditions does there exist an abstract (n+1)-polytope R whose facets occur in exactly two isomorphism types, represented by P and Q (in the semiregular/facet-intransitive sense intended in the paper, so that each ridge of R is incident with one facet of each type), and when can such an R be chosen finite?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at one of the paper’s open problems about building higher-rank abstract polytopes from two prescribed facet types. The paper is not about convex realizations, so 'polytope' should be read abstractly. The draft is incomplete because it suppresses the rank condition on P and Q, the higher-rank nature of the sought object, the two-facet-type/facet-orbit interpretation, and the local ridge-incidence condition that is normally part of such semiregular questions. I have therefore kept the question narrow and close to the apparent intent of the paper, while making it mathematically stand-alone and faithful to the abstract-polytope setting. Because the available interfaces exposed the paper metadata and companion talk material but not the full article text, this is the nearest paper-faithful reconstruction rather than a verbatim extraction of the problem statement.
